evidence.title: Testament machine-readable architecture
evidence.claim_supported: Records the approved research-foundation system shape, authoritative-data model, invariants, and service boundaries.

evidence.title: RFC-0003 Raw capture
evidence.claim_supported: Proposes exact accepted bytes, layered derived representations, bounded chunks, and parse-independent custody.
evidence.environment: Proposed normative draft; not accepted or certification-eligible.

evidence.title: RFC-0004 Provenance-preserving evidence graph
evidence.claim_supported: Proposes immutable source-linked records and distinct observations, assertions, decisions, enforcement, and audit.
evidence.environment: Proposed normative draft; not accepted or certification-eligible.

evidence.title: RFC-0006 Findings
evidence.claim_supported: Proposes findings as untrusted assertions that cannot directly select or claim enforcement.
evidence.environment: Proposed normative draft; not accepted or certification-eligible.

evidence.title: RFC-0007 Analyzer runs
evidence.claim_supported: Proposes immutable analyzer provenance, bounded execution, explicit sovereignty, and no silent fallback.
evidence.environment: Proposed normative draft; not accepted or certification-eligible.

evidence.title: RFC-0009 Policy decisions
evidence.claim_supported: Proposes ordinary denial and the narrowly qualified degraded allow-and-audit behavior.
evidence.environment: Proposed normative draft; not accepted or certification-eligible.

evidence.title: Threat, privacy, sovereignty, and key-custody research
evidence.claim_supported: Records in-review threats, controls, residual risks, trust boundaries, sovereignty profiles, and runtime limitations.
evidence.environment: Informative research candidate awaiting independent review.

evidence.title: Prototype claim-to-result ledger
evidence.claim_supported: Links each disposable prototype conclusion to its active result, observation, inference, uncertainty, limitation, pending reviewer, and superseded evidence where applicable.
evidence.environment: Harmless synthetic fixtures; pinned plan and local or PostgreSQL 17 prototype harnesses.

evidence.title: PostgreSQL backend-disconnect durability evidence
evidence.claim_supported: Three PostgreSQL 17 samples terminate an exact active fault backend and verify automatic rollback from a fresh connection within unchanged resource budgets.
evidence.environment: Harmless synthetic rows; PostgreSQL 17.11 on declared port 5440 with fresh service lifecycle and container-cgroup accounting per sample.

evidence.title: Clean-clone prototype reproduction report
evidence.claim_supported: Preserves 27 passing clean-clone samples and exact comparisons for all nine precommitted prototype and benchmark pairs.
evidence.environment: Darwin arm64 host, Go 1.26.4, Python 3.14.7, PostgreSQL 17.11 where declared.

claims.claim: one statically linked Go application with role-separated runtime modes
claims.observation: The approved machine architecture records one artifact and role-separated runtime modes.
claims.inference: Implementation and release plans should preserve one distributable while separating high-risk runtime credentials by role.

contradictory_evidence.statement: One artifact does not demonstrate that every role is safe to run with one identity.
contradictory_evidence.effect: The role-separation qualification remains mandatory.

claims.uncertainty: No production build or role-isolation test exists during the research foundation.
limitations: This is an approved design constraint, not release evidence for a built executable.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the implementation or prototype under review.

claims.claim: PostgreSQL 17
claims.observation: The approved architecture names PostgreSQL 17, and the disposable storage, durability, and replay prototypes ran against PostgreSQL 17.11.
claims.inference: Later production schemas may target PostgreSQL 17 while retaining application-layer confidentiality controls.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Small disposable prototype results do not establish production sizing, WAL confidentiality, backup behavior, or maintenance performance.
contradictory_evidence.effect: The claim remains a database choice, not a production-readiness result.

claims.uncertainty: Production schema, migration, load, backup, and failure behavior remain unimplemented.
limitations: PostgreSQL is trusted for durability, not plaintext confidentiality.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the PostgreSQL prototypes or production schema.

claims.claim: same-origin API and embedded console
claims.observation: The approved machine architecture records a same-origin operational API and embedded console.
claims.inference: The later console should use the operational service boundary rather than a separate data-bearing origin.

contradictory_evidence.statement: No operational API or console has been built or security-tested in the research foundation.
contradictory_evidence.effect: The claim describes planned topology only.

claims.uncertainty: Authentication, CSRF, CORS, session, and deployment behavior remain future implementation work.
limitations: Same-origin topology alone does not prove a secure browser boundary.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the operational surface under review.

claims.claim: separate static site
claims.observation: The approved machine architecture records a separate static standards surface.
claims.inference: Rendered standards may publish repository sources without creating a path to organization deployment data.

contradictory_evidence.statement: A future site build could accidentally add remote requests or a runtime data dependency.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Network and asset checks remain release-blocking.

claims.uncertainty: The production standards-site build and deployment do not yet exist.
limitations: A repository document is not evidence that the eventual deployed site is static or isolated.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the rendered site under review.

claims.claim: exact accepted source bytes
claims.observation: The approved architecture and RFC-0003 candidate independently record exact accepted source bytes as authority.
claims.inference: Parsing and semantic work must retain links to immutable source bytes and cannot replace them.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Filesystem readback prototypes do not prove HTTP entity-boundary behavior or production persistence.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Exactness remains a design invariant pending implementation conformance.

claims.uncertainty: Transport-layer acceptance, resumability, encryption, and production export remain unimplemented.
limitations: Authority excludes TLS records and HTTP transfer framing.
Successful custody does not imply successful parsing or semantic understanding.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the raw-capture RFC or exact-byte prototype.

claims.claim: versioned projections that never rewrite source or prior history
claims.observation: The approved architecture, evidence-graph RFC, and offline-replay prototype all preserve append-only revision history.
claims.inference: Reprojection, late events, corrections, and improved analyzers should append linked records.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The replay prototype covers only a synthetic ordered snapshot and digest method.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Production historical correctness remains unproven.

claims.uncertainty: Database constraints, API behavior, retention, and concurrency for historical revisions remain future work.
limitations: Append-only logical history does not mean every storage byte is physically immutable forever.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the evidence-graph RFC or replay prototype.

claims.claim: Content-bearing source and derived data is encrypted in the application before SQL.
claims.observation: The approved architecture requires application-layer encryption, and the disposable compression/encryption prototype proved only the precommitted operation order and tamper rejection.
claims.inference: A later envelope specification and implementation must keep plaintext and data-encryption keys out of PostgreSQL surfaces.

contradictory_evidence.statement: An authorized or compromised runtime can observe plaintext while processing it.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Application encryption must not be described as end-to-end protection against the runtime.

claims.uncertainty: No production envelope, nonce lifecycle, KMS integration, WAL scan, backup scan, or crash-path validation exists.
limitations: The prototype's deterministic nonce is prototype-only and unsafe for production reuse.
Application-layer encryption does not protect plaintext from the authorized runtime.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the encryption prototype or future envelope implementation.

claims.claim: All tenant-owned state is organization-scoped.
claims.observation: The approved architecture and threat research require organization scope across tenant data, keys, jobs, credentials, caches, quotas, indexes, policy, findings, audit, and exports.
claims.inference: Every later tenant resource and execution path must carry server-derived organization context and defense-in-depth isolation.

contradictory_evidence.statement: RLS cannot protect against arbitrary SQL by a compromised privileged runtime.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Organization predicates, role separation, encryption, and tests remain necessary in addition to RLS.

claims.uncertainty: No production tenant tables, RLS policies, pooled-connection tests, or cross-organization black-box tests exist.
limitations: Single-organization deployment must still use the same organization-scoped path.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the future tenant-isolation implementation.

claims.claim: External inference requires an explicit sovereignty profile.
claims.observation: The approved architecture, analyzer-run RFC, and sovereignty research all require an explicit profile before an external trust-boundary transition.
claims.inference: Setup and every egress attempt must fail closed rather than infer an external-provider default.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Provider declarations cannot prove hidden provider behavior.
contradictory_evidence.effect: A configured profile is an attributable declaration, not cryptographic proof of provider internals.

claims.uncertainty: No setup flow, signed attestation, egress broker, or external-analyzer implementation exists.
limitations: This feature performs no external inference and establishes no provider-conformance claim.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the sovereignty or egress implementation.

claims.claim: Analyzer output is an untrusted assertion and never directly enforces policy.
claims.observation: The approved architecture and proposed findings and analyzer-run RFCs separate analyzer assertions from policy decisions and enforcement.
claims.inference: The host must validate output and deterministic policy must decide outcomes.

contradictory_evidence.statement: A model or classifier score may be useful evidence but cannot establish that an action was enforced.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Decision and actual-action records remain separately required.

claims.uncertainty: No universal analyzer contract, output validator, policy engine, or protected-server verifier exists.
limitations: Passing analyzer evaluation cannot by itself support an enforcement claim.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the analyzer or policy implementation.

claims.claim: Unavailable or indeterminate safety checks allow and durably audit a degraded outcome only while core trust and durability remain healthy.
claims.observation: The approved architecture and proposed policy-decision RFC record ordinary denial, narrow degraded allow, durable audit, and core-failure exclusion as distinct cases.
claims.inference: Every later surface must label qualifying degraded actions without calling them safe, passed, approved, or successfully evaluated.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The decision-durability prototype proves one transaction boundary, not process-death, storage-fault, receipt, or distributed-enforcement behavior.
contradictory_evidence.effect: No release claim is supported until full failure-path implementation tests pass.

claims.uncertainty: Setup acknowledgement, runtime semantics, receipts, reporting, and fault behavior remain unimplemented.
limitations: Core identity, durability, audit, signing, or tenant-resolution failure does not qualify for degraded allow.

review.independence: Reviewer must not author the policy or decision-durability implementation.

claims.claim: Native Droid integration is out of scope.
claims.observation: The approved architecture explicitly excludes native Droid integration.
claims.inference: Repository contracts, build, conformance, and release evidence cannot depend on a native Droid runtime.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Factory tooling may assist repository work without becoming a Testament runtime or public dependency.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Tooling provenance does not authorize product integration.

claims.uncertainty: Future repository automation must still be scanned for accidental runtime or package dependencies.
limitations: This exclusion does not prohibit ordinary contributor tools that leave no product dependency.

review.independence: Reviewer must not count self-declared tooling evidence as product evidence.

claims.claim: The disposable harness can hash the committed giant fixture with bounded 64 KiB reads and preserve its byte count and digest.
claims.observation: Three clean-clone samples processed 1,100,055 bytes in 17 bounded reads and matched the independent SHA-256 within the precommitted budgets.
claims.inference: The measured read pattern is a viable input to later streaming design.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The 2 MiB-class synthetic case does not predict 1 GiB or concurrent production ingest.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Production streaming release gates remain open.

claims.uncertainty: Release-size fixtures, concurrency, parser modes, and backpressure remain unmeasured.
limitations: This is informative prototype evidence, not production or certification evidence.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: The disposable filesystem harness preserves all six committed byte classes exactly.
claims.observation: Every clean-clone sample round-tripped empty, binary, invalid UTF-8, CRLF, malformed, stream, and all-byte inputs.
claims.inference: Exact-octet custody is feasible without parsing or normalization.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Filesystem readback does not prove an ingest API contract or HTTP authority boundary.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Production exact-byte conformance remains release-blocking.

claims.uncertainty: API, CLI, encryption, persistence, resume, and export paths remain unimplemented.
limitations: The result is limited to the committed synthetic fixture set.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: The disposable Go harness compresses before AES-256-GCM, reads back exact bytes, and rejects a one-bit ciphertext mutation.
claims.observation: Every clean-clone sample reported compression-before-AEAD, exact readback, and tamper rejection within fixed budgets.
claims.inference: The operation order and authenticated readback can inform a later envelope specification.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The prototype uses a deterministic nonce and does not establish key custody or a production envelope.
contradictory_evidence.effect: The prototype must not be imported into production and cannot satisfy crypto release gates.

claims.uncertainty: Nonce lifecycle, chunk AAD, entropy failure, key rotation, KMS, crash, SQL, WAL, and backup paths remain unproven.
limitations: Application encryption is not end-to-end protection against the runtime.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: PostgreSQL 17 can store the synthetic bytea-only rows in monthly range partitions and prune the unused partition for the pinned query.
claims.observation: Each clean-clone sample observed 200 rows, two partitions, no named plaintext content column, and only the August partition in the plan.
claims.inference: Range partitioning and ciphertext-only content columns are viable inputs to later schema design.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Column inspection cannot prove every SQL, WAL, backup, log, or future write path remains ciphertext-only.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Full persistence-surface scans remain release-blocking.

claims.uncertainty: Throughput, maintenance, scaling, migration, backup, restore, and failure behavior remain unmeasured.
limitations: The result is a 200-row disposable proof, not production sizing evidence.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: The disposable HMAC harness gives stable same-scope equality and separates organization, field, and generation scopes.
claims.observation: All clean-clone samples matched within one scope and changed fixed-length tokens across organization, field, and generation.
claims.inference: Narrow organization- and field-scoped equality search is feasible.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The small synthetic proof does not measure collision probability or operational reindex behavior.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Rotation, reindex, concurrency, and leakage tests remain release-blocking.

claims.uncertainty: Normalization, token migration, query APIs, collision bounds, and no-gap rotation remain unimplemented.
limitations: Equality and frequency leakage remain within each organization, field, and generation.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: The disposable rewrap harness changes wrapped DEK material while leaving payload ciphertext and source identity unchanged.
claims.observation: Every active version 2 sample independently read persisted payload ciphertext before rewrap and after the new wrapped DEK and checkpoint, then recomputed equal payload digests and lengths, distinct wrapped-DEK digests, generations [1,2], and checkpoint 1.
claims.inference: Root rewrap without payload re-encryption is feasible for later design.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The proof does not cover interruption, dependencies, legal holds, or any cloud KMS.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Provider and production rotation conformance remains release-blocking.

claims.uncertainty: Resumption, concurrency, dependency checks, retirement, restore, and provider calls remain unimplemented.
limitations: No cloud KMS interoperability claim is supported.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: A real PostgreSQL backend disconnect automatically rolls back a uniquely identified open transaction after a separate control connection terminates that exact backend.
claims.observation: Every version 2 sample observed an active transaction and readiness marker, acknowledged exact-backend termination, a lost client with nonzero exit, backend disappearance, one committed triplet, zero faulted rows, zero orphans, and automatic rollback from a fresh connection.
claims.inference: An atomic persistence boundary with database-managed disconnect rollback is feasible for later decision design.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The proof covers backend disconnect only, not process death, host crash, storage loss, WAL corruption, fsync behavior, signing, or distributed enforcement.
contradictory_evidence.effect: End-to-end decision durability remains unproven.

claims.uncertainty: Process and host failure, storage durability, idempotency, signing, receipt return, core failure, audit verification, and protected action behavior remain unimplemented.
limitations: Only backend-disconnect rollback is demonstrated.
Issuing a decision or receipt does not prove actual enforcement.

review.reviewer: non-author security, deployment, and performance reviewer
review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: POSIX subprocess controls can bound the measured environment, directory, CPU, address space, descriptors, time, and output, but do not prove network denial.
claims.observation: Every clean-clone sample enforced the precommitted ambient and resource bounds while reporting network denial and hostile multi-tenant isolation as unproven.
claims.inference: A plain subprocess is insufficient as the complete hostile-extension isolation boundary.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The prototype explicitly cannot test operating-system network denial or a separately brokered sandbox.
contradictory_evidence.effect: No-content-egress and hostile multi-tenant isolation claims are blocked.

claims.uncertainty: WASM, brokered subprocess, seccomp or sandbox, network policy, and cross-platform behavior remain untested.
limitations: No hostile multi-tenant isolation or no-content-egress claim is made.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.

claims.claim: Pinned PostgreSQL snapshots reproduce the same digest and a late event creates a distinct superseding run without deleting prior history.
claims.observation: Each clean-clone sample retained three linked runs, matched both pinned replay digests, and changed the late-event revision.
claims.inference: Append-only replay and explicit late-event supersession are feasible design inputs.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The proof covers only a synthetic ordered snapshot and digest method, not scheduler fairness, crashes, or production windows.
contradictory_evidence.effect: Production replay and longitudinal recovery remain release-blocking.

claims.uncertainty: Lease fencing, retries, cancellation, late-event concurrency, retention, and restore remain unimplemented.
limitations: Recorded equivalence is limited to the pinned synthetic input and digest method.

review.independence: Reviewer did not author the prototype or benchmark.
